subject: Post-demo: encryption model & BYO keys — next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Linden <sara.linden@arborclinical.com>
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@arborclinical.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: encryption model & BYO keys — next steps

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — really appreciated the focused questions on key ownership and compliance. I wanted to capture the technical items we agreed to explore and propose concrete next steps so nothing gets lost in threads. Short summary of the ask from your side:

- Confirm whether Arbor requires customer-managed keys (BYOK) for PHI workloads (HIPAA) or if a Redwood-managed CMK is acceptable for non-PHI services.
- Verify SOC 2 Type II timing and whether you need our most recent report + bridge letter.
- Clarify data residency needs for EU-based patients (if you have EU data flows).
- Start the vendor security questionnaire intake so your security team can mark us as a supplier.

Redwood notes / how we can help:
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ everywhere; mTLS option for private endpoints.
- At-rest: AES-256 with envelope encryption. By default keys are Redwood-managed in our KMS; we support customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) via import or via Cloud KMS linking and an HSM-backed KEK.
- BYOK options:
  - Customer-supplied key material imported into Redwood KMS (you retain ownership, but we hold the keys encrypted in our HSM use-case),
  - External KMS bridge where Redwood calls your KMS (KMIP/CloudKMS) for crypto operations,
  - HSM-based with dual-control/escrow — used for highest-assurance PHI scenarios.

Open technical questions for your security team (if you can confirm):
1) Do you require hardware-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/140-3 HSM) for key creation and signing?
2) Are key rotation policies defined by you or should we apply our default rotation cadence (90 days for KEKs)?
3) Do you need audit events delivered to your SIEM (we can stream key-use events to a customer-owned CloudWatch / Splunk endpoint)?
4) Is there an expectation for offline key escrow?

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll loop in our encryption SME (Karthik) and compliance lead (Neha) to set a 30-min technical workshop to walk BYOK options and map to your procurement timeline.
- I attached a short one-pager that lays out the tradeoffs of the three BYOK patterns and an initial answers workbook for your security questionnaire.

Would 30 minutes on Wed 6/23 or Thu 6/24 work for a technical workshop? I can do Wed 9:00–11:30am PT and Thu 1:00–4:00pm PT.

Thanks,
Marcus
VP, Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_kms_options-onepager.pdf - PDF)
(attachment: Arbor_QS_answers_draft.xlsx - XLSX)
From: Sara Linden <sara.linden@arborclinical.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: encryption model & BYO keys — next steps

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from our side:

- HIPAA/PHI: yes, any service that will persist PHI needs customer-managed keys (BYOK) and preferably HSM-backed keys.
- SOC2: we need your latest Type II report and any bridge letters for the last 6 months.
- EU data: we do have a small EU cohort; for now we just need assurance that keys and key operations for that dataset can be restricted to EU region.

We’d like the Wed 6/23 slot at 9:30am PT if that’s available — to include our security architect (Tom) and procurement contact who will walk through the questionnaire.

I’ll start the vendor security questionnaire intake on our side and share the doc prior to the workshop. I also put a note in our procurement tracker: https://procurement.arborclinical.com/rfq/1122

—Sara
Director, Information Security
Arbor Clinical

Perfect — booked Wed 6/23 09:30am PT. Karthik and Neha are on the invite. For clarity, here’s what we’ll cover in the 30-minute workshop:

Agenda (30m):
- 5m: Goals & scope (Arbor constraints: HIPAA + EU residency)
- 10m: BYOK patterns (imported key material vs. KMS bridge vs. HSM escrow) + demo of key-use flow
- 10m: Audit, rotation, and SIEM integration (what logs we can share)
- 5m: Action items & procurement timeline (questionnaire gating items)

Pre-work for Arbor (if possible):
- Share the vendor questionnaire or a link to it before the call.
- Confirm the specific EU region requirement (e.g., eu-west-1) and whether key material must be created there.

Karthik — filing the items below as talking points for the workshop: HSM options (BYOK import vs. external KMS call), recommended rotation cadence, key lifecycle events stream. Neha — will follow up on SOC 2 artifact request and list typical attachments we provide (report + bridge + penetration test summary).

Thanks everyone — will send the calendar invite and a short pre-read.

Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Linden <sara.linden@arborclinical.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tom Becker <tom.becker@arborclinical.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: encryption model & BYO keys — next steps

Hi Sara / Tom — quick technical notes ahead of the workshop so the call can be focused:

1) If you require HSM-born keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 or 140-3) we’ll need to validate the exact compliance bar and whether you require onsite key ceremonies. Redwood supports HSM-backed KEKs and can integrate with customer HSMs via KMIP, or we can broker a cloud HSM instance dedicated to your account.

2) For EU-only key creation: we can pin key creation and key-use endpoints to the eu-west-1 region and ensure key material never leaves-region; we’ll need a short region-scoped network allowlist for the managed-control-plane to call the key operations.

3) Key rotation: we typically recommend automated rotation for data encryption keys and manual rotation for KEKs unless you’re using an external KMS. We can document rotation workflows and provide a sample KMS policy.

4) Audit trails: we can provide key-use logs (timestamp, operation, requestor) and optionally push them to your SIEM or a read-only bucket. We can also produce a signed audit snapshot if you need periodic attestation.

Attachments shared for pre-read: redwood_kms_options-onepager.pdf (attached by Marcus) and a short questionnaire draft I started populating (Arbor_QS_answers_draft.xlsx). Please flag anything missing and we’ll add it before the call.

Regards,
Karthik
Principal Applied Crypto — Redwood Inference
